questions.text: In SDEdit, what generally happens when you add more noise to the source image before starting reverse denoising?

options.A: The source is preserved more exactly because the reverse chain is longer.
options.B: The model gains more freedom to change the image, reducing source fidelity.
options.C: Only masked pixels change, regardless of whether a mask is supplied.
options.D: The model no longer needs a learned denoiser to produce an edited image.

questions.explanation: A higher starting noise level destroys more source information. Reverse denoising then has greater creative freedom but typically preserves less of the original image; this does not inherently enforce a mask.

questions.text: You need to remove a small sign from a product photo while keeping all pixels outside the edit region identical. Which workflow directly fits?

options.A: Generate a new image from a detailed text description of the photo.
options.B: Run whole-image SDEdit from a near-pure-noise starting point.
options.C: Extend the canvas and regenerate only the newly added border.
options.D: Inpaint a mask covering the sign, then composite the edited region onto the original.

questions.explanation: Masked inpainting targets the sign, and final compositing with the original explicitly preserves outside-mask pixels. Whole-image generation or high-noise SDEdit can change the product and background; outpainting targets added canvas.

questions.text: Here True marks a region to regenerate. What does this final compositing step print?
questions.code:
original = [10, 20, 30, 40]
generated = [11, 22, 33, 44]
mask = [False, True, False, True]

result = [g if m else o
          for o, g, m in zip(original, generated, mask)]
print(result)
questions.explanation: The expression selects generated values where the mask is True (positions 1 and 3) and original values where it is False (positions 0 and 2), yielding [10, 22, 30, 44].
